items.title: Derivation of Second Equation of Motion by Graphical Method

source_refs.note: Derivation of Second Equation of Motion by Graphical Method: a main subheading of 2.4 Equations of motion, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 28-28.

blocks.text: Second equation of motion can be derived using velocity-time graph for a body moving with initial velocity vi which attains a final value vf in time interval t. While moving with constant acceleration a it covers a displacement S in time t.

blocks.alt: Velocity-time graph. The straight line AB rises from A on the velocity axis (OA = vi) to B (BD = vf). Dashed lines run from E to B, from A to C (length t) and from B down through C to D on the time axis; a double arrow beside BD marks vf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.6: Velocity-time graph (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.6).

blocks.text: It can be seen from the graph that distance travelled by the body is, S = v × t.

blocks.text_alt: Also S = Area of the figure OABD

blocks.latex: S = (\text{Area of the rectangle OACD}) + (\text{Area of the triangle ABC})
blocks.text_alt: S = (Area of the rectangle OACD) + (Area of the triangle ABC)
